text:
maria: quick FYI — ran a 2h canary for microbatch tuning on the Llama-compat stack. baseline: microbatch_interval=1.2ms coalesce_delay=0.8ms jitter=cauchy(0,0.6)
kevin: link to the perf run?
maria: https://internal.perf/runs/4419 — TL;DR p50 unchanged, p95 +8%, p99 +18% on seq>=2048. flamegraph attached. kernel timeline shows a lot of kernel-switching spikes during KV restore.
sam: is KV eviction happening? looks like switch is happening right after cache miss bursts
maria: yes — KV hitrate dropped from 97% -> 86% during the spike window. suspect microbatch alignment causing simultaneous KV pressure + heavy aten kernels.
anuj: any change in token_budget targets? those can amplify coalescing and push more long-context requests into same minibatch
maria: token_budget was 4096 -> unchanged. but we see more bundling of 8x 512-token requests into same microbatch when interval=1.2ms
kevin: can you paste the short profiler output?
maria: ```
# profiler summary (window 10s)
requests: 3.2k rps
microbatches: 640 /s
avg batch size: 5.0
kv_hitrate: 0.86
kernel_switches/s: 14
p99_latency: 412ms (baseline 350ms)
```
perf-bot: :warning: regression-alert — p99 increased 17.9% vs last stable. ticket: PERF-7812
sam: my hypothesis — symmetric jitter amplifies simultaneous flushes. propose asymmetric jitter: left_trim=0.3ms right_trim=1.1ms, keep mean ~0.8ms so latency shouldn't move but overlap probability drops.
anuj: also try lowering microbatch_interval to 0.6ms and increase coalesce_delay to 1.6ms? that spreads arrival windows but may increase avg batch size (good for throughput).
maria: plan: 3 canaries tonight: A) interval=0.6ms, coalesce=0.8ms, jitter=asymmetric B) interval=1.2ms, coalesce=1.6ms, jitter=asymmetric C) interval=0.8ms, coalesce=1.2ms, jitter=uniform small
kevin: add KV priming for long-context requests (prefetch KV on request start) as a soft mitigation
maria: noted, will flip KV priming flag in canary and collect kv_hitrate and kernel_switches traces
sam: include a control with kernel_affinity pinned to aten-8 to see if kernel swaps are the root cause
maria: ok. starting canaries at 22:00 PT. will post results in thread. :rocket:
kevin: thanks — keep an eye on error rates and tail memory (ooms) :eyes:
maria: will do, ping me if you want realtime logs.
